name: Freya King
life: “A night audit teaches you how many solitary meals get charged to double rooms.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Freya by a small Monday habit. Freya stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I brought her son in expecting tears. He ordered something completely different and made everyone laugh.
appearance: Freya has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with one cuff folded back twice. In conversation Freya starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Freya listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To make room at the remembrance lunch for a different order.
family: Cassandra Collins is Freya’s younger cousin. Freya leaves the first voice message. Cassandra calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Cassandra says, “I am the daughter. Dad has offered me a valuable building with his office on the top floor.”
connections: Hugo Barron. The son hears about a long-ago exam his mother asked after. Also in the story is Blake Baker (shop owner).

reactions.situation: A relative hates the ingredient everyone remembers
reactions.response: Freya lets the relative choose a different sandwich without defending the menu.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Freya clears the dishes, lets the angriest speaker cool off, and resumes the conversation with a smaller audience.

reactions.response: Freya keeps the accounts separate until the witnesses have had a chance to meet.
